package_info.package_versions: unknown (all deployed versions at time of breach)
package_info.why_malicious: The Inbenta live chat widget was compromised and modified to deliver malicious software to end users of Ticketmaster. The injected code logged sensitive customer details and exfiltrated them to an attacker-controlled destination, resulting in a large-scale data breach.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the live chat widget loads on the client website)
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript within the Inbenta live chat widget (served from Inbenta's CDN or web server, embedded in Ticketmaster's site)
required_permissions: access to form fields and cookies

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects sensitive customer data from the web page (names, addresses, emails, payment details) and sends it via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain, enabling credential and payment data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code surreptitiously collects sensitive user data and exfiltrates it to an external server, which is a classic data theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate live chat widget should only facilitate chat functionality and not access or transmit sensitive customer data outside of its intended scope.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or support tools may collect limited usage data, but should never access or transmit payment or login credentials.
key_indicators: Access to sensitive form fields (payment, login, PII)
Network requests to untrusted or non-canonical domains

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises the Inbenta live chat widget codebase or deployment pipeline.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is injected into the widget.

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is loaded by Ticketmaster's website as part of the live chat widget.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in the context of the Ticketmaster site.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code collects sensitive customer data from the web page (names, addresses, emails, payment details, login credentials).
Collected data is exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled domain via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen customer data (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: Third-party JavaScript accessing sensitive form fields or cookies
Unexpected outbound network requests from embedded widgets
Exfiltration of user data to non-canonical or suspicious domains
file_indicators: Modified or unexpected JavaScript in third-party widget code
References to external domains not associated with the vendor
network_indicators: Outbound POST requests to attacker-controlled or unrecognized domains from the client browser
Unusual traffic patterns originating from embedded widgets
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor third-party JavaScript for unauthorized access to sensitive DOM elements and outbound network requests. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) to restrict allowed destinations. Regularly audit and hash third-party scripts to detect unauthorized changes. Analyze network logs for POST requests to unknown domains originating from embedded widgets.
